sentences.text: Counsel for the Petitioner : Mr. Gundala Siva Prasad  Reddy Counsel for the respondents : Ms. Divya Datla  Central Government Counsel ORDER:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner.
Also heard Ms.Divya Datla, learned Central Government Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents.
2. The Writ Petition is filed seeking a direction for renewal of the passport of the petitioner.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner inter alia submits that the writ petitioner practiced as an Advocate at Kukatpally, Hyderabad, till 2022.

He submits that the petitioner with a view to attend the convocation of his daughter, who completed her graduation in USA applied for renewal of passport bearing No.L2767621, which is expired on 18.06.2023.
He submits that pursuant to the application made by the petitioner, the passport authorities fixed the appointment date on 18.04.2024.

He submits that while the petitioner is ready to attend the date fixed, it is learnt that the authorities concerned would not issue the passport in the event of any criminal case is pending against the applicant.

In that regard, the learned counsel submits that a case in FIR No.760 of 2021 under Section 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 r/w. 109 of IPC was registered against the petitioner by the SHO, KPHB, Cyberabad and the same is pending.

Referring to the Memo dated 13.03.2024, the learned counsel submits that as per the certificate dated 11.03.2024 of the SHO, KPHP, P.S.,
Cyberabad, the matter is still under investigation.
Be that as it may.

The learned counsel submits Konduru Sunil vs The Union Of India, on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49217594/

sentences.text: that mere pendency of a criminal case is not a bar for issuance or renewal of passport and as it is learnt that the passport authorities are not granting the renewal unless there is an order of the Court, the petitioner is constrained to file the present Writ Petition.

The learned counsel also places reliance on the decisions in W.P No.30373 of 2022 dated 28.09.2022, W.P No.15678 of 2023 dated 04.08.2023 and W.P No.32906 of 2023 dated 05.12.2023.
4.

The learned Central Government Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents on the other hand, submits that the writ petition is premature and petitioner instead of submitting relevant documents at the time of appointed date for interview has filed the present Writ Petition and the same is not maintainable.
5. This Court has considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.

6. In so far as the issuance of passport is concerned, the law is well settled in Kadar Valli Shaik's Case1, wherein, a learned Judge had dealt with relevant case law on the subject and passed a detailed order., the operative portion of which reads as follows:-
(a) The prayer of writ petitioners seeking direction to the respondent passport authorities to renew the passport without insisting on compliance with the notification dated 2023 SCC OnLine AP 406 25.08.1993, notwithstanding the pendency of the criminal case in the Court concerned for trial, is rejected.

(b) A direction is issued to the respondents No.1 to 3 to consider the cases of the petitioners covered under clause (f) of Section 6 (2) of the Passports Act, for renewal of the passport, on production of the order from the concerned Court where the criminal case is pending for trial.

(c) On production of an order from the concerned Court, as aforesaid, the application for renewal shall not be rejected on the ground of mere pendency of the criminal case in Court, but subject to compliance of other requirements under notification dated 25.08.1993....."
7.
Another learned Judge of this Court vide Orders dated 28.09.2022 in W.P No.30373 of 2022 disposed of the same, the relevant portion of which reads as follows:-

"9. A learned Single Judge of the High Court at Madras dated 04.02.2021 in W.P.No.20058 of 2020 held that mere pendency of a First Information Report cannot be the legal basis for denial of issuance of a regular passport to the petitioner and that it is only after cognizance is taken by an appropriate Court that it can be held that criminal proceedings have commenced and issuance or renewal of the passport would be depend on no objection being given by the concerned Court.

10. The Central Government has also issued G.S.R.No.570(E), dated 25.08.1993 stipulating that a no objection order would be required from a Court only if it falls within the ambit of Section 6(2)(f)."

sentences.text:
In view of the fact that Section 6(2)(f) would arise only when there is a pending proceedings before the Criminal Court after cognizance is taken, it would have to be held that as of now there is no pending criminal proceeding before the Court."
8.
As it is specifically asserted that the matter is still at the investigation stage, in the light of the above referred decisions mere pendency of crime would not be a bar for renewal of passport.

Therefore, the Writ Petition is disposed of providing that the application of the petitioner shall not be rejected on the ground that FIR is pending and the passport authorities shall consider the petitioner's application without reference to Crime No.760 of 2021 on the file of SHO, KPHB,
Cyberabad.

Needless to mention that if the Police Verification Report (PVR) reveals that the C.C is pending against the petitioner, he has to obtain appropriate orders from the jurisdictional criminal Court where the said case is pending.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, all pending applications shall stand closed.
